items.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011
items.q: after being with Lou for about six months, the musical director who had gotten me into this gig decided he was going to go home to England. And so he suggested me to be the musical director in his place.

ctx.x: So that’s how I luckily got hooked up with Lou Rawls. And then to wrap up the story quickly, because I’ve told this before, after being with Lou for about six months, the musical director who had gotten me into this gig decided he was going to go home to England. And so he suggested me to be the musical director in his place. It’s a little bit on the unheard of side, because basically I had no credentials. I didn’t have a college education, I didn’t have a lot of experience, I mean professional experience, other…

But I did watch how Reg conducted the band and talked to him about how he wrote things, and he was also a wonderful mentor to me. He exposed me to stuff that I’d never thought of. So he said “look, just take the gig. If it doesn’t work out for you then you can go back to being the guitar player. They’re not going to fire you, and they’ll get another musical director or arranger.” Okay fine. So I did it.
